clue.text: Please put the fire out?

definitions.meaning: to please someone is to give them great pleasure
read as DE- plus LIGHT, to remove the light, as one does when extinguishing a fire

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks for a blaze to be extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to delight someone is to please them greatly; the second reading is a playful un-lighting.

clue.text: I'd help with reconstructing site of Apollo's temple

indicators.note: reconstructing means building again, so the letters of I'd help are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help rebuild an ancient Greek temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in Greece was the site of the temple of Apollo and its famous oracle.

clue.text: At Oxford, one who went up in October 1555

definitions.text: At Oxford, one who went up in October 1555

parts.words: At Oxford, one who went up in October 1555
parts.note: going up to Oxford usually means entering the university; here it means rising in the flames of execution, as a Protestant bishop did

explanation.surface: A student who started at Oxford University in the autumn of 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer, Protestant bishop, was burnt at the stake in Oxford on 16 October 1555.

clue.text: Food plant enthusiast milled to start with

indicators.note: the milled word is placed at the start, ahead of the enthusiast

parts.note: milled grain has been ground
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A keen cook grinds a crop before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut, or peanut, is a plant grown for its edible seeds.

clue.text: Neglecting consequences, as lazier philosophers did?

definitions.meaning: acting without considering what may follow
idle thinkers would have done less thinking, read as two words

explanation.surface: Idle philosophers rushed ahead without considering the results.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careless acts without considering the outcome; the second reading splits the word into past-tense think and less.

clue.text: Try and beat temptation? That's only half achieved

indicators.note: only part of each of the words beat and temptation is used, so the letters sit hidden within that phrase

explanation.surface: Resisting temptation is a struggle, and the speaker admits only partial success.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is the back half of 'beat' and the front half of 'temptation'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try, both as noun and verb.

clue.text: A state, whichever you like

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: Pick a state, any you fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Any means whichever one, no matter which, as in 'take any'.

clue.text: Start to beat in Indian rhythmic pattern? This will do

indicators.note: the first letter of beat goes inside the word for the rhythmic cycle

parts.note: tala is the rhythmic cycle in Indian classical music

indicators.note: the start of beat is its first letter

explanation.surface: To begin keeping time in an Indian rhythm, this instrument will serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: the tabla is the Indian drum used to beat out the tala.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of Indian hand drums that play out the rhythmic cycles of classical music.

clue.text: Cocktail, dress without workmanship

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dress goes around the craft

parts.note: a mini is a short dress
art is skilled workmanship or craft

explanation.surface: A badly made frock is paired with a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: What defines class, and orders levy on old motor yacht

parts.note: a levy is a tax
MY is the prefix for a motor yacht

explanation.surface: A duty is charged on an elderly pleasure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Class and order are both ranks in biological classification.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomy is the science of classification, sorting organisms into ranks such as class and order.

clue.text: Go to hill rocks with yen for such study?

definitions.text: Go to hill rocks with yen for such study?

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes, so the letters of go to hill are shaken into a new order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone longing to head for the hills to examine stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' shuffles GOTOHILL into LITHOLOG; add Y. The whole clue also describes a scientist off to study hill rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithology is the scientific study of the nature and composition of rocks.

clue.text: Regiment involved in fight needed antiseptic

indicators.note: the regiment is wrapped up inside the word for a fight

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A soldier hurt in a brawl needed something to clean the wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Borax is a mineral salt long used as a mild antiseptic and cleaning agent.

clue.text: Show great activity with a knight errant, it's said

parts.note: a busy place is said to hum with activity
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A wandering knight's band is bustling about, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb 'To err is human': being given to error is, as the saying goes, a mortal trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that erring is part of being mortal, so to be errant is, as people say, simply part of our nature.

clue.text: Period of development gutted Goole rail terminus

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: a terminus on the railway is a station

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by the state of the railway terminal in Goole.
explanation.walkthrough: Goole is a town in Yorkshire. 'gutted' looks like British slang for upset but means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the period during which an embryo develops in the womb.

clue.text: Still water in the pond?

parts.note: the pond is a jokey name for the Atlantic Ocean, and the still water is a calm, weed-filled region of it

explanation.surface: Is the water in a garden pond stagnant?
explanation.definitionFit: This region of the North Atlantic is known for its calm waters and floating seaweed.

clue.text: Religious belief is irritant in Siam, unfortunately

indicators.note: signals that the letters of irritant in Siam have come out badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A creed is said to cause annoyance in old Thailand, regrettably.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinitarianism is the Christian doctrine of God as three persons in one.

clue.text: Large guns have to be removed from Welsh town

indicators.note: the word be is taken away from the town name

parts.note: Abertillery is a town in Blaenau Gwent, South Wales

explanation.surface: Heavy weapons must be withdrawn from a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: ABERTILLERY is a former mining town in South Wales; 'have to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large-calibre guns used in warfare.

clue.text: Judge replaces Liberal in poll -a forced removal

indicators.note: the judge letter takes the place of the Liberal letter

parts.note: a poll is a vote, an election

explanation.surface: A judge takes a Liberal's seat after a vote, ousting them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejection is a throwing-out, removal by force.

clue.text: Biblical figure associated with ducking the issue?

definitions.text: Biblical figure associated with ducking the issue?

parts.words: Biblical figure associated with ducking the issue?
parts.note: ducking the issue normally means evading a question; here it is plunging people into water, baptism by immersion, done by a New Testament prophet

explanation.surface: Which character from scripture was known for avoiding difficult questions?
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament prophet baptised people, including Jesus, by immersing them in the River Jordan.

clue.text: Ancient language encountered has tense vocally indicated

parts.note: to hit upon something is to encounter it

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound and not its spelling counts

parts.note: taut and tense mean tight

explanation.surface: An old tongue is met with a strained voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hittite is the extinct Indo-European language of the Hittite empire of Anatolia.

clue.text: Person that's disliked is soon sad, unfortunately

indicators.note: the letters of soon sad have been unluckily jumbled and need sorting

explanation.surface: Someone unpleasant is soon upset, regrettably.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a mild euphemism for an unpleasant or disliked person.

clue.text: A pair together being extremely silly, zany and giddy

indicators.note: the extremes of each word, its first and last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A couple behaving very foolishly and dizzily.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy a syzygy is an alignment, and more generally a pair of connected things.

clue.text: Emotional effect of classic drama archaists translated

indicators.note: translated means converted into another form, so the letters of archaists are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lovers of the archaic render ancient Greek tragedy into modern terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle used the term for the purging of pity and fear that tragedy produces in its audience.

clue.text: One watching and protecting pheasant

definitions.meaning: a watchful guardian, after the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth set to guard Io
the great ... is a large pheasant of South-East Asia

explanation.surface: A guard dog keeps an eye on the game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant of myth gave his name to vigilant guardians and to a pheasant whose tail feathers bear eye-spots.

clue.text: Kentucky has leading pasture with unexpectedly quick drainage

indicators.note: the pasture word goes in front of the state abbreviation

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture, a poetic word
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A Kentucky meadow drains surprisingly fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that leaks lets liquid escape when it should not, draining unexpectedly fast.

clue.text: Getting on top of the Danish?

definitions.text: Getting on top of the Danish?

parts.words: Getting on top of the Danish?
parts.note: reads like mastering the Danish people or language, but means the sugary coating spread over a Danish pastry

explanation.surface: How is one coming to grips with the Danes?
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish pastry is typically finished with a sugary glaze spread over the top.

clue.text: Pop hit of the recent past?

definitions.text: Pop hit of the recent past?

parts.words: Pop hit of the recent past?
parts.note: describes a well-known Beatles single whose title is a word meaning the day before today

explanation.surface: A chart song from not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beatles song of 1965 has this title, and the word itself refers to the day just gone.

clue.text: A desire for money

explanation.surface: A craving for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong longing and also the currency unit of Japan.

clue.text: Composer rewrites lines given to opposing players

indicators.note: the letters of lines are written again in a new order

parts.note: in bridge East and North are on opposite sides, abbreviated E and N

explanation.surface: A composer revises a passage of music handed to rival performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: In backing candidacy, do by names — for example Tom, Dick or Harry?

definitions.text: for example Tom, Dick or Harry?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the run is read right to left
the letters are found within the run of words candidacy, do by names

explanation.surface: A supporter of someone's candidacy is advised to name ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'candidacy, do by names' right to left gives SEMANYBODYCA, holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick or Harry is an idiom for any ordinary person at all.
